text:
Kim: dropping a fresh direction for the latency dashboard: make the time-range header sticky but compress it into a slim bar that only shows the range label + compact sampling control when scrolled. preserves vertical space for heatmaps/p95. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/compact-sticky-range

Jordan: sounds promising. two quick thoughts: 1) how does the scrubber behave when the header shrinks? currently the scrubber sits under the header and can get hidden. 2) mobile: the compact bar may still crowd the chart at < 420px.

Nina: For the scrubber, what about keeping the scrubber in the chart layer and having the sticky bar visually overlay with pointer-events: none; then make the sampling chip pointer-events: auto. That avoids reflow but we need to ensure keyboard focus lands on the scrubber handle even if it's visually under the sticky bar.

Sam: Accessibility nits: If we use a visual clone for the compact sticky bar, the duplicate controls must be programmatically hidden (aria-hidden) except the interactive instance. Also add a role="region" aria-label="Latency controls" to the sticky bar so screen reader users can jump to it. And as Nina said, ensure scrubber handles are focusable with large hit targets (min 44px).

ContrastBot: color check: compact chip using #047AFF with white text passes AA only at 14px semibold. If we use 12px we need a darker bg. Also flag: low contrast on the slim separator line (#E8F0FF on white) fails 3:1 for decorative elements unless marked as purely decorative.

Kim: good catches. I'll move chip to 14px semibold and darken separator. Also thinking about tooltip interaction: p95 marker tooltips currently expand downward and will intersect the sticky bar. Options: A) render tooltip above sticky bar with a connector, B) push chart down by stickyHeight when sticky is active, or C) allow tooltip to overlay sticky but increase z-index and add a subtle shadow to indicate layering.

Jordan: prefer A for visual clarity. moving tooltip above feels less surprising. downside is it might overlap other UI above the header on very small screens. We could do conditional: above if space, else overlay with fade.

Nina: technically easiest is to compute available space above the data point and place tooltip where it fits (above if available, else below). When the sticky bar is present treat it as an obstacle in the placement algorithm. We should also animate placement changes but respect prefers-reduced-motion.

Sam: microcopy suggestion: change "Sampling: 1/100" to "Sampling — 1 in 100" for clarity in plain language and for VoiceOver pause/readability. Also add an aria-live="polite" span that announces "Sampling updated to 1 in 100" whenever the rate changes due to user action or auto-adjust.

Kim: we'll adopt that copy. For layout: I'm going to prototype two flows in Figma: CompactOverlay (sticky overlays chart, no reflow) and AnchorNudge (sticky nudges chart down by stickyHeight). I'll also try a hybrid option where users can toggle "Preserve chart layout" in preferences.

Jordan: nice. On keyboard nav please ensure Tab order is preserved across the sticky transition. If we duplicate the range control, only the primary interactive instance should be tabbable (remove from tab order using tabindex="-1" and aria-hidden on clones).

Nina: Tooltip connector idea: when tooltip is pushed above the sticky region, draw a 1px connector line from the marker to the tooltip to maintain context. Also make sure SVG pointer isn't clipped by overflow rules.

Sam: A11y checklist for the iteration: - aria-live for sampling updates - role=region + label for sticky bar - duplicates aria-hidden and tabindex management - focus ring visible for sticky state - test with screen readers and keyboard only - respect prefers-reduced-motion for sticky animations

Kim: action items: 1) I'll publish the two Figma variants tonight. 2) I'll push the microcopy change and chip color update to the tokens PR. 3) @Jordan can you test keyboard focus on the CompactOverlay variant? 4) @Nina can you implement the tooltip placement logic prototype in the playground? 5) @Sam can run a screen reader pass on both variants once available.

Jordan: will test keyboard flows tonight and post notes.

Nina: prototyping tooltip placement + connector in the playground by tomorrow morning.

Sam: I'll run NVDA/VoiceOver and report quirks tomorrow. Also will check that the sampling aria-live message reads cleanly when toggling quickly.

ContrastBot: recheck scheduled after token update. will validate updated token colors and the slim separator treatment.

Kim: thanks everyone. keeping this thread as canonical for the compact sticky iteration. I'll open a follow-up PR for the microcopy + color tokens once Figma variants land.

Jordan: :thumbsup:

Nina: :sparkles:

Sam: thanks!
